Required acceptance case: Clean demo installation from the documented commands, without game assets or credentials.
Two content lines with different pack sizes, finishes and reward policies work without core code edits.
The same game account receives the same collection across characters and devices; renaming does not create a new inventory.
Cross-account requests cannot read private cards, sealed outcomes, purchases, codes, claims or albums.
Repeating one purchase key 100 times concurrently creates one operation, one capture and one pack allocation.
Reusing a purchase key with a different quote returns conflict without another debit.
Two legitimate concurrent purchases cannot overspend the host balance.
Simultaneous game spending, website spending and autosave preserve the correct configured currency ledger and cache values.
Crash before/after each hold, allocation, capture and finalization boundary recovers without lost configured currency or duplicate copies.
Capture timeout after a successful host debit resolves to the original packs, with no second debit.
Hold expiration racing capture has one provider outcome; local resources reconcile accordingly.
Publication, pause and price changes invalidate/retain quotes according to the documented policy.
Every product produces exactly its configured slots; zero/negative weights and missing variants are rejected.
Exhausted unique pools and finite editions follow declared fallback or reject before capture.
Concurrent last-edition purchases cannot exceed the cap or duplicate a serial.
Batch pity transitions equal the same ordered sequence of single purchases.
Sealed allocations count consistently for configured history-based duplicate protection.
RNG source and unbiased selection are reviewed; deterministic test vectors and statistical checks match configured rules.
Closing the browser at every reveal step retains all awarded cards and permits replay.
Repeated open calls return the original allocation and historical new-card indicators.
Updating a reward pool or archiving a line cannot change an already allocated prize.
Website claim and game code entry racing each other produce one delivery.
A provider delivery accepted before timeout is looked up and never repeated under a new delivery ID.
Inventory-full, offline character and partial bundle cases remain recoverable with correct per-component state.
Expiry racing claim acceptance resolves atomically; accepted pending claims are not expired mid-delivery.
Token generation, normalization, hash lookup, encrypted reveal, revocation and key rotation behave as specified.
Public sharing, exports, logs and analytics contain no codes, private account IDs or financial details.
Album placement never changes owned quantity; concurrent edits cannot silently overwrite one another.
Official completion handles variants, missing cards and optional subsets according to its published rules.
Plugin duplicate events and downtime do not duplicate achievements or affect completed purchases.
Plugin uninstall and renderer failure preserve owned art, provenance and a usable static fallback.
Content package import rejects traversal, executable content, invalid references and conflicting stable IDs.
Upgrade from the previous supported release preserves copies, entitlements, albums and pending operations.
Restore rehearsal reconciles a stale framework backup against newer host receipts without duplicate debit or delivery.
Desktop 16:9 and mobile flows pass keyboard, touch, reduced-motion, no-audio and screen-reader checks.
Recorded load test meets the selected targets or publishes measured limits and adjusted safe configuration.
Refund interruption freezes affected assets and resumes safely; grants cannot bypass edition limits.
A new adapter passes the published conformance suite without access to reference host internals.
Catalog/economic metadata remains immutable after publication; cosmetic revisions retain their history.
An independent developer can author a new line and install the example plugin from documentation alone.
